protocol.name: acompositor_desktop_v1

description.summary: the desktop's control over windows, captures and shortcuts

protocol.description: Only the desktop gets this global: acompositor offers it on the connection the session hands it as privileged, never on connections made through WAYLAND_DISPLAY. Windows of every client are listed and controlled here; the desktop's own panels and background use wlr-layer-shell.

interface.name: acompositor_desktop_v1

description.summary: the desktop's handle on acompositor

interface.description: On bind acompositor sends a window event for every toplevel already shown, then work_area, then done. Later windows come as they are shown. From version 2 the desktop also hears the work area of every screen it has bound a wl_output for. From version 3 acompositor keeps virtual desktops: every window belongs to one desktop, only the windows of the current desktop are shown, and panels (layer-shell) show on all of them. Desktops are numbered by the desktop client; desktop 0 exists from the start and is current. New windows land on the current desktop; a window with a parent lands on its parent's. From version 6 the desktop tells acompositor how to round the corners of windows and which shadows to draw around them. From version 7 windows (acompositor_window_v1 version 5) can be made the wallpaper of a screen. From version 8 the desktop picks the cursor theme, and acompositor animates windows (opening, minimizing and restoring, state changes, desktop switches) by the motion preset the desktop picks; windows (acompositor_window_v1 version 6) take animations of their own. From version 9 it tells which window a drag of files was dropped on. From version 10 windows (acompositor_window_v1 version 7) say whether they are on the Agent's stage. From version 11 a client acompositor took at the dev level (only in a guest started by acdev) hears what the seat and the windows do: presses, move and resize requests with acompositor's answer, keyboard focus, windows shown and hidden, drags. From version 12 such a client also asks how the screen is drawn (render_state) and where a point lands (hit). From version 13 windows (acompositor_window_v1 version 8) say whether their client answers acompositor's pings. From version 14 the desktop sets windows aside (acompositor_window_v1 version 9). From version 15 the desktop sets the height of the titlebar the runtime draws on app windows. From version 16 it also sets the measures of that titlebar's controls and title.

entry.name: unknown_desktop
entry.summary: the desktop number names no desktop

entry.name: last_desktop
entry.summary: the only desktop cannot be removed

entry.name: same_desktop
entry.summary: windows cannot move into the desktop being removed

entry.name: dev_only
entry.summary: render_state and hit are for a client at the dev level only

event.name: current_desktop

description.summary: the desktop being shown

event.description: Sent on bind and whenever the current desktop changes, before done.

description.summary: make a desktop with this number; nothing happens if it exists

request.name: remove_desktop

description.summary: remove a desktop, moving its windows into another

request.description: If the desktop is the current one, into becomes current in the same step.

request.name: show_desktop

description.summary: switch to a desktop in one step

event.name: window

description.summary: a toplevel is shown

event.description: The window object gets its app_id, title, parent and state events, then done.

description.summary: the screen less the edges panels reserve

event.name: output_work_area

description.summary: one screen's work area

event.description: Sent for each wl_output the desktop has bound, when it is bound and whenever that screen's work area changes, before done. Coordinates are the compositor's logical ones, the same as wl_output.geometry. work_area stays the first screen's.

description.summary: the end of a burst of window, work_area and desktop events

request.name: capture

description.summary: capture the screen, one window, or the desktop with its panels

request.description: The capture object reports the size of the picture with buffer_size; the client then hands it an shm buffer of that size with copy.

request.name: capture_output

description.summary: capture one screen, or only its background and panels

request.description: Like capture, for the screen behind output; what is screen or desktop. A window capture, or an output whose screen is gone, gives a capture of size 0 whose copy fails.

entry.name: screen
entry.summary: everything on the screen, cursor left out

entry.name: desktop
entry.summary: the background and panel layers only

request.name: bind_shortcut

description.summary: take a key combination for the desktop

request.description: A bound combination never reaches clients. key is an evdev code; key 0 with the super modifier is Super pressed and released alone, which acompositor holds back until it knows whether another key follows.

request.name: set_keyboard_repeat

description.summary: how held keys repeat, for every client

request.description: The same meaning as wl_keyboard.repeat_info: rate is repeats per second, 0 turns repeating off; delay is how long a key is held, in milliseconds, before it repeats. acompositor starts at 25 and 600; a rate outside 0 to 100 or a delay outside 100 to 2000 is taken as the nearest bound. Every wl_keyboard and input method keyboard grab hears the new values at once. acompositor does not keep the setting across restarts.

request.name: set_pointer

description.summary: how a kind of pointing device behaves

request.description: speed is -1 to 1, 0 by default: relative motion is multiplied by 4 to the power speed. left_handed 1 swaps the left and right buttons (touchpad taps stay as they are). natural_scroll 1 turns the wheel and finger scrolling the other way. scroll_factor is 0.1 to 10, 1 by default, and multiplies finger scrolling only; a wheel moves by its clicks. Values outside the ranges are taken as the nearest bound. Mice and touchpads keep separate settings. acompositor does not keep them across restarts.

request.name: set_touchpad

description.summary: touchpad tapping and resting while typing

request.description: tap_to_click 1 makes a short touch click (one finger left, two right, three middle). disable_while_typing 1 ignores touchpad motion, scrolling and presses for 300 ms after a key other than a modifier is pressed. Both are 1 by default.

entry.name: tablet
entry.summary: a pointing device with absolute positions

event.name: input_device_added

description.summary: an input device acompositor reads

event.description: Sent for every device on bind and when one is plugged in, before done. A device that is both a keyboard and a pointer comes once for each, under its own id. Ids are not reused. Power buttons and lid switches are left out.

description.summary: a device is gone, before done

request.name: set_scale

description.summary: the scale of every screen, or back to automatic

request.description: In 120ths, as in wp_fractional_scale_v1: 120 is 1, 180 is 1.5. 0 goes back to the scale acompositor picks from the screen's density (or the one given with --scale). A value outside 120 to 480 is taken as the nearest bound. All screens share one scale, so there is no output argument. Clients hear the change through wl_output.scale, preferred_buffer_scale and preferred_scale as usual. acompositor does not keep the choice across restarts.

request.name: set_window_corners

description.summary: round the outer corners of windows

request.description: acompositor cuts the corners of every window it decorates (a shown toplevel in the normal state whose window geometry, if any, covers its surface) along the superellipse |x/r|^n + |y/r|^n = 1, letting what lies beneath show through, and does the same to the window's subsurfaces. radius r is in logical pixels, 0 to 256, 0 (the start) leaving corners square; a radius larger than half the window's smaller side is taken as that half. exponent n is 2 (a circular arc) to 8, values outside taken as the nearest bound; 4 to 5 look like a continuous corner. Popups are neither cut nor shadowed. Every window is drawn again at once.

description.summary: drop the shadow layers of one state; every window is drawn again

request.name: add_window_shadow

description.summary: one more shadow layer around the windows of one state

request.description: What one entry of CSS box-shadow draws outside a box: the window's shape (with the corners of set_window_corners) moved by x and y, grown by spread (shrunk when negative, the radius growing or shrinking with it), blurred with a Gaussian whose standard deviation is blur / 2, painted in color and left out where the window itself is. x, y, blur and spread are logical pixels: x and y -256 to 256, blur 0 to 256, spread -256 to 256, values outside taken as the nearest bound. color is ARGB8888, not premultiplied. Layers are painted in the order they are added, the first at the bottom (the reverse of a CSS list); a state keeps at most 4 layers and further ones are ignored. acompositor starts with no layers. Every window is drawn again at once.

entry.name: standard
entry.summary: a critically damped spring of response 0.35 s: scale, move and fade

entry.name: reduced
entry.summary: no scaling or moving: a 0.15 s linear fade; desktops switch at once

request.name: set_motion

description.summary: how windows animate

request.description: The parameters of each preset live in acompositor (acde_scene::motion); the desktop only picks one. acompositor starts with standard. Running animations keep their curve; later ones use the new preset. Reduced also drops the scaling and moving of animate, keeping its fade.

request.name: set_titlebar_height

description.summary: how tall app windows' titlebars are

request.description: height is in logical pixels; values outside 24 to 64 are taken as the nearest bound. acompositor starts with 32 and hands the height on to every client (in acdes over acompositor_backdrop_manager_v1.titlebar_height), whose runtime draws the frame of the windows it opens from then on that tall. Windows already open keep their titlebar.

request.name: set_frame_metrics

description.summary: the measures of the window controls and title the runtime draws

request.description: In logical pixels: inset is the distance of the controls from the edge, dot the diameter of a mac style control, gap the space between them, caption the width of a Windows style control, title_size the title's font size; title_weight is its font weight (100 to 1000). A negative value stands for the runtime's own default. The values are handed on to every client (in acdes over acompositor_backdrop_manager_v1.frame_metrics) as they are; acompositor keeps the last ones but does not read them. Until the desktop sends them, clients hear nothing and the runtime uses its defaults.

request.name: create_embed_slot

description.summary: reserved: a place in a desktop surface for another client's surface

request.description: Embedding is not implemented yet: the slot sends unavailable at once.

request.name: set_cursor_theme

description.summary: the Xcursor theme and size of the pointer

request.description: name is an Xcursor theme's folder name, looked up in XCURSOR_PATH (or the usual icon folders) and followed along the Inherits of its index.theme; size is the nominal size in logical pixels, 8 to 256, values outside taken as the nearest bound. The themed cursor on screen is drawn again at once; cursors a client gave as a surface stay as they are. A shape the theme and its parents lack falls back to the theme called default, then to a built-in arrow. acompositor does not keep the choice across restarts and does not touch the environment: whoever starts programs gives them XCURSOR_THEME and XCURSOR_SIZE.

event.name: dropped

description.summary: a drag offering text/uri-list was dropped on a window

event.description: Sent when a drag whose source offers text/uri-list is dropped on a surface of a window and the drop is performed (the same moment the target gets wl_data_device.drop). window is that toplevel. uri_list is the read end of a pipe whose write end acompositor handed to the drag's source with wl_data_source.send("text/uri-list"): the list comes from the source, not from the window, so the desktop can tell what was really dropped. Drags without a source (inside one client) send nothing.

event.name: press

description.summary: dev level: a pointer button went down

event.description: Only a client at the dev level hears this and the other events from version 11; a bind by any other client at version 11 gets none of them, and acompositor makes none while no such client is bound. Every window number in them is the N of the window's identifier acompositor-N; 0 is no window (a panel, the lock screen, the background). x and y are the pointer in the compositor's logical coordinates, window is the toplevel under it (a popup counts as its toplevel), button the evdev code.

event.name: move_request

description.summary: dev level: a window asked to be moved

event.description: accepted is 1 when the move began; otherwise 0 and reason says why.

event.name: resize_request

description.summary: dev level: a window asked to be resized

event.description: edges are those of xdg_toplevel.resize_edge; accepted and reason as for move_request.

event.name: focus

description.summary: dev level: the keyboard went to another surface

event.description: window is the toplevel that has the keyboard now, 0 when it is no window or nothing.

description.summary: dev level: a toplevel is shown for the first time
dev level: a shown toplevel is no longer shown

event.name: drag_start

description.summary: dev level: a drag began

event.description: window is the toplevel it began in; 0 for a drag acompositor began for an injected drop.

event.name: drag_end

description.summary: dev level: a drag ended

event.description: window is the toplevel it ended over, 0 when none; dropped is 1 when the target got wl_data_device.drop, 0 when the drag was cancelled.

request.name: render_state

description.summary: dev level: how the screen is drawn now

request.description: The new object reports the render backend, then every glass and frosted area of the shown windows, then done. Another client gets the dev_only error.

request.name: hit

description.summary: dev level: where a point lands

request.description: x and y are in the compositor's logical coordinates. The new object reports the surface input goes to at that point by the current stacking and input regions, the windows under it that also hold the point, then done. Another client gets the dev_only error.

description.summary: one toplevel of any client
the process that owns the window, 0 when unknown
the application the session vouched for when it handed acompositor this window's client; empty when none
the window has the keyboard (1) or lost it (0)

event.name: desktop

description.summary: the desktop the window belongs to

event.description: Sent with the window's first events and whenever it moves, before done. The window object has version 2 when the desktop bound acompositor_desktop_v1 at version 3 or later.

event.name: stacking

description.summary: where the window stands among the toplevels, from the back

event.description: 0 is the backmost toplevel; a larger place is nearer the front. All toplevels of all desktops share one order, so the windows of the current desktop compare by their places. Sent with the window's first events and whenever its place changes, before done; raising one window moves the places of those it passes. The window object has version 3 when the desktop bound acompositor_desktop_v1 at version 4 or later.

event.name: identifier

description.summary: a name for the window that stays while acompositor runs

event.description: Sent once, with the window's first events, before done. It is the same for this window on every acompositor_window_v1 object, also after the desktop binds acompositor_desktop_v1 again, differs between windows (also of one client) and is not used again while acompositor runs; like the identifier of ext-foreign-toplevel-list.

event.name: min_size

description.summary: the smallest size the client accepts

event.description: What the client set with xdg_toplevel.set_min_size, in logical pixels; 0 is no limit in that direction. Sent with the window's first events and whenever it changes, before done. The window object has version 4 when the desktop bound acompositor_desktop_v1 at version 5 or later.

description.summary: the end of a burst of events about this window
the window is gone; destroy the object

request.name: activate

description.summary: bring the window to the front and give it the keyboard (shows it if hidden, restores it if minimized; from version 2 also switches to its desktop)

request.description: A window on the Agent's stage (see the stage event) leaves the stage first: the person takes it over. It moves to the current desktop, with its dialogs and popups, and from then on is a window like any other.

entry.name: unknown_desktop
entry.summary: the desktop number names no desktop

request.name: move_to_desktop

description.summary: move the window, with its dialogs and popups, to another desktop

request.description: A window moved away from the current desktop disappears in the same step; the keyboard goes to the front window that stays.

description.summary: hide the window without minimizing it (virtual desktops), or show it again

request.name: set_aside

description.summary: keep the window out of window cycling and of the keyboard's next pick

request.description: 1 sets the window aside, as for a panel the desktop opens as a window: Super+Tab passes it over, and when the keyboard needs a new window acompositor never picks it. A click still gives it the keyboard, as for an on-demand panel. 0 makes it an ordinary window again. Only the desktop's own connection may call it; acompositor ignores the request from any other connection.

description.summary: ask the window's client to close it (xdg_toplevel.close)
move a normal window; a size above 0 also asks the client for that size

request.name: set_wallpaper

description.summary: show the window as the wallpaper of a screen

request.description: acompositor takes the window out of the stack and draws it over the whole screen, under the desktop page (layer-shell bottom) and over the plain background, and asks its client for the screen's size. It is no longer drawn as a window, cycled to, or given the keyboard, and listings leave it out; the object stays and sends wallpaper 1. A window made the wallpaper of a screen that has one already sends the old one back. The window object has version 5 when the desktop bound acompositor_desktop_v1 at version 7 or later.

arg.name: pointer
arg.summary: 1: it gets pointer input where nothing is above it; 0: it gets none

description.summary: send the window back to the stack as a normal window, in front, at its old size

event.name: wallpaper

description.summary: whether the window is a wallpaper now

event.description: 1 after set_wallpaper took; 0 when it is a normal window again: unset_wallpaper, another window made the wallpaper of the same screen, or the screen went away. Sent before done.

event.name: stage

description.summary: whether the window is on the Agent's stage

event.description: 1 while the window is on the stage: a toplevel of a program the Agent started, kept off every screen and out of the person's stacking, cycling and keyboard. To its client it stays shown: it keeps its wl_surface.enter, frame callbacks and the activated state, and shots of it work. Its desktop number takes no desktop. 0 once it is a window of the person's desktops, as after activate. Sent before done, with the first burst only when it is 1.

event.name: unresponsive

description.summary: whether the window's client answers pings

event.description: acompositor sends xdg_wm_base.ping to a client when it hands the client input (at most once in 2 seconds) and when one of its windows is activated. 1 once a ping has gone 5 seconds without a pong: every window of that client is then unresponsive. 0 as soon as the client answers. Sent before done, with the first burst only when it is 1.

description.summary: the CSS easing keywords, as cubic Bézier curves

request.name: animate

description.summary: move how the window is drawn to a target, over a time

request.description: The window is drawn scaled by scale about its centre, moved by dx and dy logical pixels and with the opacity (0 to 1) given; fields not in the fields mask keep the value they have now, which is 1, 1, 0, 0 unless an animation left them otherwise. After delay milliseconds the values go to the target over duration milliseconds along easing; they stay there when it ends, so animating back to 1, 1, 0, 0 undoes it. Only the drawing changes: the window keeps its place for input and in geometry. A later animation of the same window, its own or one acompositor starts (minimizing, a state change, a desktop switch), replaces it, and the replaced one ends where it was. Under the reduced motion preset scale, dx and dy are ignored. animated follows when the animation ends or is replaced, also when there was nothing to do.

arg.name: fields
arg.summary: the fields given: 1 opacity, 2 scale, 4 dx, 8 dy

description.summary: an animate request ended or was replaced
one answer to render_state

entry.name: none
entry.summary: not drawn: covered by opaque windows above it

entry.name: cpu_glass_frosted
entry.summary: glass, drawn on the CPU as frost with the glass's tint

event.name: backend

description.summary: what composes the screen

event.description: device and driver are the GPU's adapter name and driver; both are empty on the CPU.

event.name: area

description.summary: one glass or frosted area of a shown window

event.description: window is the N of acompositor-N; surface is the wl_surface's id in its client. The rectangle is in physical pixels of the composed screen.

description.summary: one answer to hit

event.name: landed

description.summary: the surface input goes to at the point

event.description: window is the N of the toplevel the surface belongs to, 0 for none; role is toplevel, popup, subsurface, layer, lock or none (nothing there); surface is the wl_surface's id in its client (0 for none); sx and sy are the point in that surface's coordinates.

event.name: beneath

description.summary: a window that holds the point but is covered there

event.description: Sent for each shown window under the landed surface whose rectangle holds the point, from the nearest down.

description.summary: copy the picture into an ARGB8888 or XRGB8888 shm buffer of buffer_size
the combination is taken or not allowed; destroy the object
reserved for embedding another client's surface; not implemented
